parts.text: The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured old man with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin with age spots, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a large ear with a fat hanging lobe, thick neck, hunched broad shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Head type: a huge tall lumpy dome skull with dents and bumps, like the master reference, pink flesh-toned clay skin, wild spiky grey hair tufts, raised blue clay veins on the forehead. A carved bone skull mask with cracked teeth and hollow eye sockets. Wearing a stained torn undershirt, his right hand wears a thick grimy grey welder's gauntlet with bent rusty nails and short broken kitchen-knife blades crudely welded and taped onto the knuckles, a clenched spiked fist, knuckles toward the camera, a rusty harpoon gun slung on his back. A dark night backdrop with a huge cratered blood-red clay moon. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. His right hand grips the held weapon in a tight clenched fist seen from the back of the hand, knuckles toward the camera, palm hidden, the blade angled up and out; his other hand hangs open. POSE: his head and body are clearly turned 45 degrees to the viewer's right in three-quarter view, NOT facing the camera. The nail-knife glove is the hero of the image: a big chunky rusty work glove on his right hand, raised in front of his chest close to the camera, large and in sharp focus, its long rusty nails and knife blades jutting out over the knuckles. Keep the cracked bone skull mask with red-rimmed eyes showing through the sockets. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora
